scope: Read-only primary-source and input-contract qualification; no tests or data acquisition
review:
**Verdict: No candidate qualifies for a genuine Phase 3.5 evaluation.** The engine’s contract requires 120–1,500 contiguous XNYS sessions of raw closes and complete split/dividend records, with every complete row evidenced as available no later than 60 minutes after that session’s close. That last condition is decisive: the historical sources reviewed do not provide the required per-record point-in-time publication evidence within the cutoff. No data was downloaded, no account was created, and no provider was purchased.

| Candidate | First-party evidence and disposition |
|---|---|
| [Alpha Vantage documentation](https://www.alphavantage.co/documentation/) and [terms](https://www.alphavantage.co/terms_of_service/) | The docs describe raw daily OHLCV plus split/dividend events, with 25+ years of coverage. However, the adjusted endpoint is marked premium; full daily history is premium, while free compact history is only 100 observations, below the engine’s 120-session minimum. The default terms grant personal, non-commercial use and classify use on behalf of a firm as commercial. No documented archive of each row’s original availability time was found. **Reject: access/rights and PIT evidence fail.** |
| [Nasdaq Data Link WIKI Prices](https://data.nasdaq.com/databases/WIKIP) | First-party metadata describes daily prices, dividends and splits for 3,000+ U.S. companies, from January 1996, and says the dataset was released into the public domain. It also says support ended April 11, 2018, advises against investment or analysis, and states a 9:15 p.m. ET weekday update cadence, after the engine’s regular-session 5 p.m. ET cutoff. The page returned 404 when opened during this review; the details were available in Nasdaq’s search-indexed metadata. **Reject: stale, late, and without the required row-level PIT evidence or verified raw-price/action-completeness methodology.** |
| [Tiingo EOD documentation](https://www.tiingo.com/documentation/end-of-day) and [terms](https://app.tiingo.com/tos/) | The API documents raw and adjusted prices plus `divCash` and `splitFactor`; Tiingo says its checks help catch missing corporate actions. It reports most U.S. EOD prices available at 5:30 p.m. EST, with exchange corrections through 8 p.m., beyond the close-plus-60 cutoff. Its terms’ model-validation/backtesting permission requires an active Power or Power Commercial subscription and restricts outputs to internal use rather than a third-party service. **Reject: availability and rights do not fit this evaluation.** |
| [NYSE TAQ Closing Prices](https://www.nyse.com/data-products/catalog/taq-nyse-closing-prices), [NYSE historical products](https://www.nyse.com/market-data/historical), and [Market Event Feed](https://www.nyse.com/market-data/corporate-actions/market-event-feed) | TAQ Closing Prices documents daily OHLC/last and volume as of the 4 p.m. close, with history from November 2001. Corporate actions are a separate product/feed. The pages direct users to purchase access and do not establish close-plus-60 delivery or archived per-record publication times. **Reject: paid access and PIT evidence are unresolved.** |
| [CRSP US Stock](https://www.crsp.org/research/crsp-us-stock-databases-2025-layout/) and [CRSP research products](https://indexes.morningstar.com/research-data-products) | CRSP describes daily data and corporate actions across active and inactive U.S. securities, with research-grade historical coverage. Access is subscription-based; the reviewed material does not establish per-record first-publication timestamps meeting this contract. **Not available under the no-purchase constraint and not PIT-qualified here.** |
| [Stooq terms](https://stooq.com/t/?i=1) and [historical-data page](https://stooq.com/db/h/) | Both first-party pages presented a JavaScript browser-verification screen. I did not bypass it or fetch market data. **Unqualified: first-party rights, raw-versus-adjusted basis, corporate actions and PIT evidence could not be verified.** |

The repository records the same blocker in [PHASE3.md](C:\stock price predictor\docs\implementation\PHASE3.md) and [RESEARCH-OPERATIONS.md](C:\stock price predictor\docs\implementation\RESEARCH-OPERATIONS.md): synthetic fixtures establish pipeline behavior, not empirical performance. The contract requires the complete row’s availability between exchange close and close plus 60 minutes; it also explicitly says a retrieval timestamp alone is insufficient evidence.

There is a provenance limitation in the current implementation worth preserving in the acceptance decision. `dataset.py` checks supplied timestamps and an operator-supplied `corporate_actions_complete` flag; it cannot verify that those declarations match an archived provider record. `ResearchDataset` stores the normalized payload, its canonical-content version hash and an import `created_at`; it has no separate raw-source-file hash or acquisition-time field. Accordingly, the normalized dataset hash is not evidence of the original download’s bytes or timing. The project docs also caution that licensing and historical truth are operator-supplied, not independently proven by import.

A bounded `.local` filename check found no CSV, Parquet, Feather or Arrow candidate. I did not inspect the modified SQLite database or credentials. **No dataset was accepted, so there are no genuine historical results, raw-data hashes or acquisition dates to report.** The one-session and five-session baselines remain numerical reference methods only; the existing synthetic results must stay labelled as pipeline checks, and no legacy model gains empirical acceptance from this review.

This was a read-only source qualification; no project files were changed and no tests were run. The minimum evidence for a later import is a lawfully held raw archive and terms covering storage, private research, backup/transfer and intended use, plus source-authenticated availability history for both prices and actions proving each row met the unchanged close-plus-60-minute cutoff. Until then, preserve the pipeline and report empirical qualification as blocked.
